A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GROUTER research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining, downstream evaluation, throughput measurements, routing analyses, and architectural and expert-folding ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Small-Qwen3 results and a smaller-source-to-larger-target transfer experiment.

M1.justification: Section 3.2.2 introduces Expert Expanding, extending adaptation beyond v1's expert merging. It identifies underserved tokens, clusters their representations, projects and orthogonalizes new routing directions, and appends them to the score matrix. This adds a substantive procedure for targets with more experts than the source.

E1.justification: The data and task coverage remains C4 pretraining and the six downstream benchmarks BoolQ, RTE, HellaSwag, PIQA, RACE, and MNLI. The added experiments change model configurations and source-target relationships without introducing different datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Figure 4 retains the same comparison methods, including Aux Loss, Aux Loss Free, Z Loss + Aux Loss, Balanced Hash, StableMoE, ReMoE, TopP, and MoE++. The added Small-Qwen3 and cross-scale comparisons use the existing Z Loss + Aux Loss comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 256-expert Small-Qwen3 configuration trained for 50B tokens. Appendix O adds a protocol that pretrains a 550M Tiny-Qwen3 source for 30B tokens and evaluates its distilled router on Mini-DS-V2-Lite over 20B tokens. These are localized additions; retained experiments keep their existing settings and metrics.

E4.justification: New Appendix O tests whether a smaller source can supply useful routing structure to a larger target. New Appendix P analyzes storage requirements and the computational costs of the complete routing pipeline. These substantially extend the practical feasibility analyses beyond v1's retained architecture, folding, and stability studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing gradient-variation analyses and their sliding-window settings are unchanged; v2 adds no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing results are retained. Table 1 adds Small-Qwen3 validation losses of 1.648 for GROUTER and 2.633 for ZL after 50B tokens. Figure 12 adds comparable convergence with a smaller source model. Table 5 newly estimates total pipeline cost at 721,149 TFLOPs, reported as 19.11% of baseline cost. These substantially extend the reported findings rather than revise existing scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds mathematical definitions for projection and expanded weight assembly in Equations 6–7, plus a sparsity-adjusted computational cost model and stage-specific derivations in Appendix P. The routing-interference and gradient-cancellation reasoning in Appendices A and N remains unchanged apart from equation numbering.

C1.justification: The new conclusion explicitly includes Expert Expanding among the framework's contributions, extending the stated adaptation mechanisms. The central decoupling claim and headline claims of 4.28× data efficiency and up to 33.5% throughput acceleration are retained.

C2.justification: Appendix O interprets the new experiment as supporting transfer from smaller sources. Appendix P argues that storage is manageable and preprocessing costs can be amortized or overlapped with idle resources. The future-work discussion adds a proposed hardware-fault-tolerance benefit. Existing explanations of specialization and routing stability remain intact.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link and a statement that code and checkpoints are publicly released, whereas v1 only promises release. It also documents the expanded expert configuration, GROUTER's hidden width, and quantitative caching and cost assumptions. Existing hardware, software, and baseline details are retained; moving the setup into Section 4.1 is not a technical change.

R1.justification: New Appendix E adds discussion of LLM development and knowledge distillation, distinguishing routing-structure extraction from task-knowledge compression. Additional citations include Elastic MoE, distillation, and fault-tolerant optimization work. The existing positioning against static routing and jointly learned routing remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental setup moves from Appendix E to Section 4.1, Appendix E becomes related work, and v2 adds a conclusion and acknowledgments. Affiliation and publication-header text also changes. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands to four model columns and becomes full-width; Figure 8 gains a fourth panel. v2 adds Figure 12 and Table 5 and relocates several existing displays through pagination. All original figure panels are retained unchanged, so the visual revision is localized.

improvement.justification: The expansion experiment and smaller-source transfer test address concrete applicability gaps in v1, while the release link improves reproducibility information. The overhead analysis adds useful accounting, but its 2.4B distillation-token assumption is unreconciled with Section 4.1's retained 2.6B setup, and its costs are estimates rather than measured full-pipeline runtime. The additions support a limited overall improvement.
